open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: a path with a trailing slash added is redirected to the route's path
open_points.question: What exact redirect status, Location form, body and headers must be returned, and must the original query string be preserved?
options: 307 with a relative Location, the query string preserved and the framework's default body and headers
308 with a relative Location and the query string preserved
301 or 302, allowing a client to change the method
An absolute Location derived from the request instead of a relative Location
open_points.default_guess: Use the framework default 307 redirect, preserve the method and query string, and point Location at the same path without its final slash.

witness.initial: The surface is serving and the caller has no redirect cached.
events: The caller sends POST /v1/projects/01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef/photos/deliver/?trace=1 with a valid token and body.
outcomes: The surface answers 307 with Location /v1/projects/01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef/photos/deliver?trace=1, so a conforming client repeats POST.
The surface answers 302 or 308, or emits a different Location form or drops trace=1; the caller follows or reports a different response.
witness.observer: The calling flow and any HTTP client or reverse proxy observing the response

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: a path with a trailing slash added is redirected to the route's path. Any other path answers 404, and a route's path with another method answers 405
open_points.question: When both the trailing-slash rule and the wrong-method rule apply, does the surface redirect, answer 405 at the slash-added path, or answer 404?
options: Redirect first, preserving the wrong method; the target then answers 405 if followed
Normalize the path for matching and answer 405 immediately
Treat the slash-added path with the wrong method as an unmatched path and answer 404
open_points.default_guess: Redirect first and preserve the method; answer 405 only after the client requests the canonical path.

witness.initial: The surface has GET /health and no POST /health route.
outcomes: The caller receives the trailing-slash redirect to /health.
The caller receives 405, or 404, without a redirect.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: A path matches a route only as the table writes it
open_points.question: Is matching performed against the raw request-target spelling or against the server/framework's percent-decoded and normalized path?
options: Match the framework's decoded path, so percent-encoded unreserved characters can match route literals
Match the raw path spelling, so only the literal route spelling matches
Define an explicit subset of percent encodings and normalizations that may match
open_points.default_guess: Use the framework's decoded path matching without additional raw-path enforcement.

outcomes: The decoded path is /health and the caller receives the health answer.
The raw spelling is not the table's /health and the caller receives 404.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: `{project_id}` and `{source_id}` each standing for one path segment
open_points.question: Are segment boundaries determined before or after percent-decoding reserved characters such as `%2F`?
options: Decode before routing, so an encoded slash creates another segment and the path does not match
Split the raw path first, so `%2F` remains inside one captured value and the handler later validates it
Reject encoded path separators explicitly before route matching
open_points.default_guess: Use the framework's decoded path; an encoded slash creates a segment boundary and this request answers 404.

events: A caller sends GET /v1/projects/01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abc%2Fdef/photos with the correct token.
outcomes: Percent-decoding creates an extra path segment, so the surface answers 404.
Raw splitting captures one project_id value, so the handler runs and answers the invalid-project-id M08 response.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: with the framework's own body and not M08
open_points.question: Are all headers of 404 and 405 responses delegated to the framework, and in particular what exact Allow header must a 405 response carry?
options: Delegate the complete response to the framework, including Content-Type, Content-Length and Allow
Require only the framework body and status, leaving headers to the implementation
Specify the allowed method in Allow while delegating all other headers
open_points.default_guess: Delegate the complete default 404 or 405 response to the pinned framework, including its Allow header.

witness.initial: The surface has only GET /health at that path.
events: A caller sends POST /health and inspects the response headers.
outcomes: The 405 response includes Allow: GET and the framework's other default headers.
The response has the same status and body but omits Allow or supplies a different set of headers.
witness.observer: The caller and any HTTP middleware enforcing method negotiation

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.question: Must create_app prevent generation and programmatic access to a route description, or must it only stop serving description endpoints over HTTP?
options: Disable only /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc while allowing the returned application object's schema-generation method to describe the routes
Disable or override schema generation as well, so no generated route description is obtainable from the returned object
Permit an internally generated cached schema provided it is never served
open_points.default_guess: Disable all HTTP schema and documentation endpoints, but leave the framework's programmatic schema method unused and available.

witness.initial: deliverer_service has received the application object returned by create_app, and no HTTP documentation endpoints are registered.
events: An in-process caller or test invokes the framework's schema-generation method on that application object.
outcomes: It receives a generated description of the four routes even though no HTTP path serves it.
Schema generation is disabled and no description is returned.
witness.observer: deliverer_service, an in-process extension or a test inspecting the returned application
